region.text: the three governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok that the Region holds as a federal region

events.note: The Kurdistan Region page gives 'Federal region established: 15 October 2005' and says the Region 'comprises four Kurdish-majority governorates' (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok and Halabja, the last cut out of Sulaymaniyah's cells). The 1 January 2010 anchor draws all three as plain Iraq with the Region owning no land, against the dossier's own 1992-2013 keyframe; this restores them from 2010 (a no-op if the 2000-2009 window already did).

region.text: the disputed territories the Peshmerga held from June 2014 (Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar, Makhmur, Zummar and the Mosul Dam area), outside the three governorates

events.note: Iraqi forces moved on the disputed territories from 16 October 2017: 'On 31 October, Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi announced that Iraq had regained control of all disputed areas'; the Region 'lost 40% of the land mass it had administered prior to the conflict'. The dossier's Kurdistan Region ledger covers only parts of the zone by place name; the other cells of the 2014 keyframe's discs (30 cells) were set to nobody by the 2018 keyframe snap. [Reviewer: Iran is no longer cut from this region: the Khanaqin disc's cell 196094 (34.34N 45.47E) lies in the gazetteer's Iran but was Iraq's at the p2010 anchor; the Region took it from Iraq in June 2014 (its ledger/3), and with the Iran cut it stayed the Region's to 2020. The gain moves only cells the Region holds, so it goes back to Iraq with the rest.]

region.text: Salah ad-Din and At-Ta'mim, the last Islamic State cells in Iraq outside the governorates the ledger already returned

events.note: 'On 9 December 2017, Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi announced victory over the Islamic State' (War in Iraq 2013-2017). The 2017 keyframe leaves the Islamic State no land in Iraq but the ledger never returned the rest of Salah ad-Din (59 cells) or one At-Ta'mim cell, so the snap left them as nobody's land for ever. The pages opened do not date Baiji or Shirqat earlier, so the return is dated to the declared end of the war.

Closes the wrong-way relation (Turkey's own land 'occupied by Syria') that Turkey's ledger/7 opens when its circles take in Turkish cells north of the border. The page's infobox calls the zones 'Syrian territories under military occupation of Turkey'.

region.text: Jarabulus and its border district, Syrian land

events.note: The page's infobox calls the zones 'Syrian territories under military occupation of Turkey'. Operation Euphrates Shield was 'Established during the First offensive: 24 August 2016' and on 26 August 2016 a civilian council condemned 'the occupation of Jarabulus'. The Islamic State ledger hands the district to Turkey, but the land is Syria's under Turkish occupation.

region.text: Jarabulus and its border district, Syrian land

events.note: The page's infobox calls the zones 'Syrian territories under military occupation of Turkey'. 'The Syrian National Army captured an area of 2,225 square kilometres during Operation Euphrates Shield' (established 24 August 2016).

region.text: al-Bab and its district, Syrian land

events.note: The page's infobox calls the zones 'Syrian territories under military occupation of Turkey'. The page gives no capture date for al-Bab (only a de facto military governor 'since 2017'); the date is that of the Islamic State ledger's entry (23 February 2017), which this event does not change, only the owner it hands the land to: Syria, not Turkey.

region.text: the three cells in Pará that the Antilles' 1986 shape still holds

events.note: The page lists the Netherlands Antilles as 'the Leeward Antilles islands of Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire' and 'the Leeward Islands of Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten', all Caribbean islands, dissolved on 10 October 2010. The p2010 anchor still gives the Antilles three cells in Pará (Brazil) on the Suriname border, left over from the old Suriname/Guyana mask; the dissolution of 10 October 2010 would turn them into nobody's land, so they go back to Brazil first.

region.text: the cell by Paramaribo that the Antilles' 1986 shape still holds

events.note: The page lists the Netherlands Antilles as 'the Leeward Antilles islands of Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire' and 'the Leeward Islands of Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten', all Caribbean islands, dissolved on 10 October 2010. The p2010 anchor still gives the Antilles one cell next to Paramaribo (Suriname), left over from the old Suriname mask; it goes back to Suriname before the dissolution.

correction.text: the Region after the Peshmerga took 'most disputed areas, including Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar and Makhmur' in June 2014; the discs around Khanaqin and Sinjar are cut at the frontiers with Iran and Syria

keyframe_overrides.why: The 2014 keyframe's 45 km disc at Khanaqin and Jalawla and the 45 km disc at Sinjar cross the frontiers: five cells of Iran's Kermanshah and one of Syria's Hasakah fall inside the shape; they were drawn as Kurdistan Region land from 2014 and then dropped to nobody by the 2018 keyframe. The page says only that the Peshmerga took 'most disputed areas, including Kirkuk'; no Iranian, Syrian or Turkish land.
